chapter: Growing up in the Brubeck family
title: Chris on realizing his father's work was unusual: riding to gigs with Dave
summary: Chris recalls rubbing Dave's injured back on drives home from concerts and parents who encouraged but never pushed music.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Did that sort of leadership skill of avoiding conflicts, was he like that as a father? I guess my question was prompted from last night when you were talking to the audience you said people often ask us what was it like to be a Brubeck kid or the Brubeck family. And you said, “Well it’s the only family we did so I can’t really answer that.” But, I was wondering first of all, you must have learned what the word gig meant at an early age. And your friends probably didn’t know what the word gig meant. Did it occur to you, or
at what age did it occur to you that my father and my mother are engaged in a business that most people are not.

Well I can say for me, one of my specific early memories is that, as you probably know Dave really messed up his back, broke his back, broke his neck in this diving accident in the late 40s in Hawaii. And so his back was always, you know, just a time bomb waiting to screw up and so he would say like, “I have a concert” and it would be not too far away. And he would just say, “Does anyone want to come with me?” And I remember I liked it and I said, “Yeah I’ll come with you.” And he said, “But yeah, on the way back from the gig you’ve got to sit in the back seat and you’ve got to rub my shoulders to help me be able to drive back.” That was like part of the deal. I’d say, “Okay.” And then I remember going to the concert and then seeing Dave and Joe and Gene and Paul playing to like a thousand people or fifteen hundred people, whatever it was, and see them going nuts and hear that great music and from a very early age I thought well this is an attractive, wonderful way to lead your life. You know? It’s interesting. And of course we know other families where there’s great musicians and they had the complete opposite thing, the parents, you know, weren’t a model because they weren’t in the arts. You know? “What are you crazy? You should be a doctor or a lawyer.” You know? And those people would fight against their heritage in order to become musicians. And in our case my parents wouldn’t have been disappointed if we weren’t musicians. And the other thing people imagine like maybe Dave was there with Iola with whips like Simon Legree like, “You must practice.” You know. They weren’t like that either. They encouraged us but they weren’t disciplinary about it.
